assessment.nobel_worthiness: The opening of neutrino astronomy: a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, a clear clue from nature rather than an elegant idea. It gave a new window on cosmic-ray accelerators and has an existential flavour I find compelling.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led IceCube for two decades and is the only credited name, which makes a clean single-laureate configuration. Whether the committee would want a second name for the early detector concept or for the key analyses is unresolved; I cannot verify the finer history of who proposed what.
assessment.maturity: The 2013 observation has been confirmed by multiple analysis channels, by the 2017 blazar coincidence, and by NGC 1068 and Galactic-plane evidence in the 2020s. Timing looks right, though source identification is still partial.
uncertainties: Credit within a very large collaboration and the role of earlier pioneers (DUMAND, Baikal, AMANDA) would need outside expert reports.
Some source associations are statistically moderate, so the mature core is the diffuse flux itself.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a whole field of topological materials. The prediction was sharp and was tested by a decisive experiment in HgTe, so theory and nature meet.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental demonstration (building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, which is not among the credited names here). That gives a natural theory-plus-experiment trio, though the omission of Zhang or Bernevig is an unresolved fairness issue.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations (HgTe, Bi-based 3D materials with ARPES), and a stable interpretation after roughly twenty years. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The BHZ proposal and Zhang's role could complicate the allocation.
Technological applications remain modest, so the case rests on conceptual impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle flat bands with correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created moire quantum materials as a new platform. The prediction of the magic angle was followed by an unexpected experimental result, which is the kind of clue from nature I value.
assessment.attribution: MacDonald (with Bistritzer) predicted the flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery in 2018. I propose the two principals. Including Bistritzer would be possible but I treat the junior-author question as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Extensively reproduced by many groups, but the microscopic origin of the superconductivity is still debated. The field is young, which weighs against it.
uncertainties: Possible need to recognise the experimental co-lead (Cao) or other early theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto), not supported by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement of a large theta-13 closed the last gap in the three-flavour mixing picture and opened the way to CP-violation searches in the lepton sector. A discovery first, and a precise one.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay (Wang, Luk) and RENO (Kim) announced nearly simultaneously in 2012. The trio is credible and fair to the two Asian experiments. Double Chooz and the earlier T2K indication are not credited names, which weakens the picture somewhat.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation from several experiments and a stable result in all later global fits. Timing is good after the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2015 prize may make the committee wary.
Priority between experiments and collaboration-scale credit need expert input.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Kilonovae link neutron-star mergers to r-process nucleosynthesis, and the GW170817 counterpart is a spectacular observational confirmation of a theoretical prediction. It speaks directly to where heavy elements come from.
assessment.attribution: Metzger and Kasen made the central theoretical predictions and models; Tanvir is credited for observational discovery in the GRB 130603B/GW170817 context. Credit is spread, with many observers and other theorists (Li and Paczynski) unrepresented.
assessment.maturity: The GW170817 counterpart is a single exceptional event with strong multi-wavelength support; no second clear event, so confirmation is less independent than I would like.
uncertainties: Heavy involvement of astronomy rather than physics proper, and large collaboration credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background opens a new band beyond LIGO and may probe supermassive black-hole binaries or new physics. Very exciting, and relevant to my cosmology interests.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed over several PTA collaborations (NANOGrav, EPTA, PPTA, CPTA, IPTA), and the three names are a coarse selection. I cannot confirm they are the decisive contributors.
assessment.maturity: The signal is at about 3-4 sigma with consistent evidence across collaborations, but the astrophysical origin is unclear. This looks premature for now.
uncertainties: Source interpretation (binaries versus cosmological) is open.
Allocation across collaborations is very hard.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductors was an unexpected result that created a second family of high-Tc materials and challenged assumptions about pairing.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the original LaFeAsO(F) discovery; Chen and Zhao's groups rapidly raised Tc. Hosono's claim is clearest, and a three-person list is plausible but the later improvements are arguably incremental.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed and widely studied, but no consensus on the pairing mechanism and Tc is below cuprates, which limits long-term impact compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the Tc-raising work deserves equal weight with the original discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, with the magic-wavelength idea and later realizations, have pushed timekeeping to the 10^-18 level, opening tests of fundamental constants, relativity and geodesy. A clear invention with demonstrated performance.
assessment.attribution: Katori invented the optical lattice clock concept; Ye's group realised leading performance. A fair two-person configuration, though the ion-clock and comb contributions (already recognised in 2005 and 2012) remain adjacent.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many labs. Redefinition of the second is still pending, and the Nobel connection to earlier clock prizes might make it feel incremental.
uncertainties: Competing claims from Lemonde, Pfau, Ye and Katori on the early ideas cannot be verified by me.
